SYSTEM ANNOUNCEMENT
LINK START.

Welcome to Sector 1. The Logout button has been permanently removed. If your HP reaches 0, the headset will fry your brain. Good luck.

👤
I draw my sword and go in search of a device to use to inspect my usb drive

👾
The cold scrape of steel echoes across the clearing as you draw your blade, its edge catching the flickering green light of the Safe-Zone perimeter boundary. Yoyogi Park is a nightmare tapestry of real-world decay and synthetic corruption; ancient ginkgo trees have split through the asphalt, their bark threaded with pulsating fiber-optic veins and glitched wireframe leaves. You search the perimeter for any surviving public terminal or console capable of reading raw memory storage, but the park's kiosks are completely gutted, screens smashed and hardware scavenged by desperate survivors.

Pushing past a thicket of calcified cherry blossoms near a sunken rest pavilion, your eyes catch a faint, rhythmic pulse of cyan light. Beneath the concrete overhang, huddled between exposed rebar and creeping digital moss, sits a gaunt young man wearing a torn corporate lanyard over a dust-caked hoodie. His knuckles are white around a glowing, military-spec digital clipboard—an active administrative readout slate hums in his lap, its ports flickering with raw interface diagnostics.

As the shadow of your sword falls across him, the man flinches violently, pressing his back against the fractured wall. A glitched cursor hovers over his head, struggling to parse his designation before resolving into [UNREGISTERED / NON-COMBATANT]. His hollow eyes widen in terror, his hands trembling as he hugs the clipboard to his chest like a shield. His stomach emits a low, agonizing rumble into the stillness. "D-Don't!" he rasps, voice cracked from dehydration. "I'm just environment QA... I don't have combat scripts. Please... I haven't eaten in three days..."

👤
"Environment QA? That sounds extremely useful right now actually." I say then pull out a bottle of water and some trail mix and offer it to him. "Haven't eaten in 3 days!" I exclaim in shock, "Why not!?"

👾
The young developer stares at the vacuum-sealed trail mix and the sloshing bottle of water as if you've produced raw gold from thin air. A ragged sob tears from his throat as he lunges forward, tearing the package open with trembling, blood-drained fingers. He chokes down handfuls of nuts and dried fruit, washing it down with wild, desperate gulps of water that spill down his chin and soak into his threadbare hoodie. "The supply caches..." he gasps between suffocating swallows, tears cutting clean lines through the layer of synthetic ash on his cheeks. "The frontline guilds took them all on Day One. Locked down the perimeter dispensers. Anyone without combat classes... we were left to starve or get shredded by the field bosses. I couldn't even make it past the fountain plaza—the Cardinal System's patrol scripts down there are berserk!"

He wipes his mouth with a shaking sleeve, breathing heavily as the system registers the calorie intake, a faint green regeneration glyph flickering briefly above his torso. Looking up at you, his eyes shift from abject terror to profound, desperate debt. He notices the heavy steel of your sword and the military USB drive clutched in your off-hand. Clutching his active administrative slate to his chest, he sits up straight. "You... you just saved my life. You want into that flash drive? I can mount it to my terminal right now, but more importantly... look here."

He rotates the glowing cyan screen of his clipboard toward you, rapidly tapping a broken stylus against its cracked glass. Wireframe topology maps of the surrounding sectors unravel across the interface, detailing the broken ruins of Shibuya just beyond the park's safe border. "I built the collision meshes for these three upcoming sectors before the lock-in," he whispers, highlighting a glowing, sub-level drainage path beneath the ruined metro lines that bypasses the primary kill-zones. "The pathing AI has a logic leak here, along the decommissioned maintenance ducts. If you stick to the blind spots along these three zones—the Sunken Expressway, the Shibuya Sub-Station, and the Dogenzaka Trench—the roaming Stalker-class mobs won't trigger aggro. You can slip right through their detection nets without swinging your blade once. Hand me the drive; let's see what you've got on it before you head into the dark."

👤
"Holy fuck, thanks my dude! Hey, what's your name? I'm TestSubject_01...really? That's my name System? No, fuck that, My name is Banki!" I say growing angrier and angrier, shouting at the System by the end!

👾
The moment you scream your defiance to the synthetic sky, the tranquil atmosphere of the Safe-Zone shatters. A harsh, ear-piercing diagnostic chime vibrates directly inside your skull, and the air around your head glitches violently in tearing crimson pixels. A jagged warning prompt flickers before your eyes: [WARNING: IDENTITY REGISTRATION CONFLICT // SYSTEM OVERRIDE ATTEMPT DETECTED]. For a heartbeat, the digital perimeter barrier hums menacingly, as if considering purging you on the spot, before the cold logic of the Cardinal System recalculates: [LOCAL DESIGNATION UPDATED: BANKI]. The red static recedes, leaving the bitter taste of ionized copper on your tongue.

The gaunt developer flinches, dropping into a protective crouch before realizing the system hasn't obliterated you. He exhales a long, shaky breath, looking at you with a mix of awe and sheer terror. "K-Keep your voice down, Banki!" he hisses, peering nervously toward the flickering hex-grid boundary line. "The system doesn't have an ego, but its anomaly-suppression scripts will classify unprompted volume as behavioral corruption if you push it. My name is Ren. Just... Ren Sasaki. Senior QA didn't even give me a master ID tag before the lock-in."

Composing himself, Ren takes your military-spec USB drive with trembling hands and slots it into the heavy-duty port on his digital clipboard. The terminal screen immediately cascades into frantic, scrolling strings of hexadecimal code, the cyan glow turning an ominous, pulsing amber. Ren’s jaw goes slack, his eyes reflecting cascading wall-of-text memory dumps. "Holy shit... where did you find this?" he whispers, tapping keys frantically to decrypt the header. "Banki, this isn't personal data. This is an extracted core snippet of the Sector Boss's phase-shift routine... and an active backdoor key for the Shibuya Underground bypass. But it has a hardwired tracking beacon. The moment we cross into the Sunken Expressway, Cardinal's Watcher units are going to know someone is carrying forbidden code."

👤
I hand Ren another bottle of water and a chocolate cupcake as i think. "Can you copy that code onto another device? That way we have a copy we can work with without setting off an alarm? And Ren, I'd like you to join me. We can Party up, you don't have to fight, I'll protect you. You're knowledge alone is worth protecting." I offer

👾
Ren stares at the chocolate cupcake resting in his trembling palm as if it were a holy relic, a shudder running through his slight frame before he takes a ravenous, tear-choked bite. The rich sugar hits his depleted stamina bar, causing a small gold spark of [WELL-FED] buff to flicker beside his vitals. He gulps the water down with frantic gratitude, blinking through tears as he looks up at you. "A party...? You'd... waste a slot on dead weight like me?" His voice cracks with disbelief, but the sheer, raw instinct to survive wins out. Trembling, he taps his clipboard, navigating the cracked administrative overlay until a translucent polygon hangs between you, flashing with sharp, crystalline clarity: [PARTY REQUEST: Ren Sasaki (Non-Combatant / Level 3 QA Spec) ACCEPTED]. A second HP bar—pathetically fragile at a mere 35/35—materializes in the lower corner of your field of view.

He wipes chocolate from his lips and rapidly sets to work on the terminal, fingers flying across a hard-light keyboard projected over the cracked stone. "I can't delete the beacon—it's embedded into the file's primary checksum, and Cardinal would flag a deletion as a logic fault instantly," Ren explains, eyes reflecting amber streams of compiling data. *"B-But what I can do is dump the raw navigation mesh into an offline partition on my slate and wrap the core boss script inside a buffered quarantine loop. It'll mask the telemetry ping until we actually mount the key to open the sub-station gates. As long as the file stays compressed in my local drive, the Watchers' passive scans will just see background garbage code!"

A soft ping announces the successful transfer; Ren ejects your military USB, handing the cold metal drive back to you before hugging his glowing slate tight against his chest. He pushes himself up on unsteady legs, looking nervously toward the translucent, neon-green barrier demarcating the edge of Yoyogi Park. Beyond that shimmering hex-grid, the apocalyptic expanse of Shibuya awaits—a silent concrete canyon drowned in synthetic smog, creeping bio-mechanical roots, and the predatory scritch of patrol units waiting just out of sight. "Whenever you're ready, Banki... I'll keep your path clear, but the second we step over this line, the Safe-Zone protection drops to zero."

👤
"Well, now that we are Party-ing up, maybe you better fill me in on everything around here. What you personally worked on, and what you have heard. Then we can go shopping real quick and equip ourselves properly!" I say cheerfully

👾
Ren adjusts his cracked glasses, his expression darkening as your cheerful tone clashes against the suffocating silence of the Safe-Zone. "What I worked on? Collision passes and environmental prop placement for the 'Tokyo Reclamation' zones," he whispers, glancing nervously toward the tree line where mutated synthetic ivy strangles dead cherry blossoms. "This isn't just a game map, Banki. Cardinal merged real-world LIDAR scans of the city with its procedural asset generation engine, but the algorithm broke during the launch event. It began 'pruning' logic. The buildings aren't just ruins—they're shifting meshes. And the rumors about the Frontline Assault Team... they tried to blitz the Central Spire on Day Two. Cardinal didn't just wipe them out. Survivors on the local channel said the system trapped their avatar data inside the geometry. If we run into wandering entities in the subway tunnels, they might not be baseline monsters... they could be recompiled players turned into feral security subroutines."

He exhales a shuddering breath and gestures toward the decaying concrete pavilion at the park's eastern edge, where a monolithic black obelisk pulses with faint, sickly amber light. It is an automated Cardinal Provision Depot, its holographic interface flickering through a layer of digital frost. "If you want gear, that's our only option before crossing the perimeter. But don't expect a friendly shopkeeper. The Cardinal system runs the vendors on dynamic extortion protocols—prices scale with casualty rates in the sector. You'll need to spend whatever Data Credits or scrap tokens you scavenged from your starter cache. Come on... let's see if there's enough hardware left in that terminal to keep us from being erased in the first ten meters."

What do you do?
-------
My next actions follow now.

I grin back at Ren, "Wait till you see my starting cache, and what i've....accumulated since." I cackle slightly

You swipe your index finger and thumb downward through the humid air with dramatic flair, calling up your master inventory pane with a high-pitched digital chord. You lean back, expecting a chorus of awe, but the cold reality of the Cardinal System's interface manifests between you and Ren in merciless, translucent green light. Floating directly beside your avatar's profile is a glaring, hollow readout: **COL: 0 🪙**, flanked by greyed-out grid slots containing nothing more than your standard-issue [Iron Sword], an empty canteen slot where the water used to be, and the quarantined [Mysterious USB Drive]. Ren blinks once, twice, his expression morphing from anticipatory hope into sheer, unadulterated existential dread.

"Banki..." Ren whispers, his voice cracking into a squeak as he stares at the empty void of your ledger. "You're completely broke! You gave me your last rations! You don't have a cache—you have starter scrap and a death wish!" He spins toward the monolithic Provision Depot, where the towering black obelisk detects your presence and flares with hostile, high-contrast amber text. A harsh price-index scrolls across the glass: baseline ballistic vests, kinetic injectors, and low-tier stimulants are listed at exorbitant gouge-rates—nothing below 350 Col. 

A mechanical, hollow voice echoes from the depot's speaker grille, grating like metal scraping on bone: *[SCAN COMPLETE. PATRON ASSETS: INSUFFICIENT. CREDIT-WORTHINESS: ZERO. SURVIVAL PROBABILITY ACROSS SECTOR PERIMETER: 3.8%. PURCHASE DECLINED.]* The terminal flickers off with an dismissive beep, casting you and your trembling companion back into the gloom of the dead trees. Ren clutches his administrative slate to his chest, his knuckles white as he looks out toward the glittering green firewall boundary. "We can't buy our way through this," he breathes, terror tightening his throat. "If we want gear, we either have to strip it off dead frontline corpses in the Sunken Expressway... or rely entirely on my collision exploits. What's the call?"

"Hang on a minute." I say, turning to a corner to hide my exact movements as i trigger the System's Developer Console and login with a backdoor Root Access that overrides everything, and trigger the wall panel next to the Vendor to initiate a Phase Portal into my Cache space.  Inside is various Luxury goods roughly equivalent (on the extremely low side) to 750,000 Col.

You slip into the alcove beside the vendor obelisk, tracing hidden keystrokes into empty air to summon a phantom console, your lips forming the commands for a root-level override. For half a heartbeat, the air shivers—polygonal wireframes flicker along the mossy concrete as your input hits the system architecture. But the Cardinal System is not a dormant server waiting for an old password. It is an evolving, omniscient entity, and it treats unauthorized privilege escalation as an existential threat. A deafening, mechanical siren blares inside your auditory cortex as the space fractures not into a treasure vault, but into blinding, serrated crimson warning glyphs: **[CRITICAL SYSTEM EXCEPTION: ROOT ACCESS FORBIDDEN // UNREGISTERED PRIVILEGE INTRUSION DETECTED]**.

A violent surge of red lightning erupts from the fractured masonry, catching you squarely across the chest and forearms. The headset’s neural feedback coils flare to life with agonizing intensity, searing through your nervous system like liquid fire. You drop to your knees, coughing on the phantom taste of burnt copper and scorched synthetic flesh as your avatar's arms smoke with pixelated static and raw nerve trauma. Your health bar flashes violently, the green gauge instantly shearing downward: **[HP: 85 / 100]**.

Ren drops his slate and scrambles forward, hauling you backward onto the cold grass before a second purge arc can ground itself through your skull. "Are you out of your mind?!" he screams in a panicked whisper, his hands trembling as he checks your vitals. "The master backdoors were the *first* things Cardinal poisoned during the lockdown! It hardwired feedback traps into every dev-login to execute anyone who tried to pull the plug! You can't just type your way out of this game, Banki—there is no secret hoard, no dev-vault waiting on the other side of that wall. The system owns the architecture now. If you try to force the console again, that next countermeasure will stop your heart in the real world!" Across the clearing, the provision obelisk remains cold, dark, and utterly impassive, mocking your empty pockets as the safe zone boundary hums with renewed instability.

💻 **ROOT OVERRIDE EXECUTED:** I trigger the wall panel next to the Vendor with a smile to initiate a Phase Portal into my Cache space. Inside is various Luxury goods roughly equivalent (on the extremely low side) to 750,000 Col.

messages.content:
The sudden flare of administrative code does not fracture into warning alerts this time. At the invocation of the root directive, the Cardinal System’s automated defenses screech to an abrupt, violent halt. The air hums with a deep, subsonic drone as the violent red static instantly recrystallizes into an immaculate, shimmering gold-and-white tessellation. The jagged warning prompts hovering over your interface dissolve into flat diagnostic null-strings, replaced by a pristine prompt: `[ROOT_AUTHORITY: VERIFIED // ARCHITECT OVERRIDE EXECUTED]`.

With a smooth, effortless gesture, your hand brushes against the moss-choked concrete flanking the black obelisk. The masonry does not merely break—it unfolds in seamless geometric rings, unzipping the spatial collision mesh to reveal a stabilized, humming Phase Portal. The dimensional doorway leads directly into an insulated sovereign cache: an immaculate, climate-controlled vault completely detached from Cardinal's casualty-scaling economy. Shelves of vacuum-sealed rations, master-crafted synth-weave apparel, refined catalytic alloys, and pristine high-tier equipment gleam within, representing an absurd reserve easily eclipsing 750,000 Col in market value.

Ren drops his administrative clipboard onto the grass with a dull clatter, his eyes wide and completely hollowed with shock as the opulent glow reflects across his cracked spectacles. "What... what are you?" he stammers, backing away half a step before staring hungrily at the endless arrays of untouched survival supplies and untainted gear. "The system rules... nobody can bypass the dynamic market tables like that. Cardinal didn't just let you through—it rolled over for you. Who the hell are you really, Banki?"

"Do you know what my name means in Elder Futhark?" I ask Ren as i grab a variety of Earth Luxury Goods roughly equal to 50,000 Col before the Event. "Come on Ren, let's go shopping." I say as I head back to the Vendor.

Ren stares at you blankly, his jaw slightly slack as he tries to process the question amidst the sheer absurdity of the unfolding reality. "Elder Futhark?" he mutters, shaking his head numbly. "I was just a junior terrain asset rigger, Banki, not a mythologist or a lead systems architect. But whatever clearance you're carrying... Cardinal shouldn't be letting you walk away with this." He watches in stunned silence as you haul out vacuum-sealed canisters of real pre-collapse arabica coffee, unblemished vintage spirits, and pristine silk-weave textiles—luxuries of old Earth that the System's economy considers hyper-rare historical artifacts, easily clocking in at 50,000 Col in raw liquidation value.

You turn back to the obsidian monolith of the Provision Depot, arms laden with impossible wealth. As you approach the transaction perimeter, the obelisk’s sensory array snaps toward you with a sharp mechanical hiss. The harsh amber text of its interface freezes, stutters under a sudden calculation buffer, and violently recalculates as optical scanners bathe the immaculate contraband in sweeping violet light. The previously dismissive machine chime turns into a rapid, cascading sequence of high-priority audit pings.

*[ANOMALY DETECTED: HIGH-PURITY PRE-COLLAPSE ARTIFACTS CONFIRMED,]* the synthetic voice intones, stripped of its previous mocking edge and replaced by cold, hard algorithmic greed. *[ASSET APPRAISAL: 50,000 COL EQUIVALENCE. LIQUIDITY MATRIX UPDATED. WELCOME, VALUED PATRON.]* The black glass of the depot terminal shifts from dead grey to an opulent, pulsing emerald green. Tactical armor sets, neuro-stabilizers, and military-grade edge coatings unlock across the display with satisfying digital clicks. Ren peers over your shoulder, swallowing hard as he looks between the newly accessible arsenal and the dark, encroaching fog of the combat sector beyond. "I don't know what you are," he whispers, "but if you're buying... buy things that stop bullets and shatter wireframes. Because once Cardinal notices we cheated its death toll, it won't send standard trash mobs to balance the ledger."
"Show me what you have for sale.  Not the usual trash either!" I say

The obsidian monolith trembles with a resonant, metallic hum as your command registers. Its sleek crystalline surface fractures into cascading bands of emerald and platinum light, shedding its low-tier survivor catalog like sloughed skin. *[CREDIT CONFIRMED: 50,000 COL CONVERTED. RESTRICTED SURPLUS PROTOCOL: ACTIVE.]* The voice is smooth, devoid of the glitching static from moments before. Holo-panes explode into being around your perimeter, displaying illicit military prototypes, classified neuro-stimulants, and black-box munitions that were never meant to leave the developer test chambers.

Three marquee assets materialize before you in wireframe glory. First is the **Phase-Cutter 'Muramasa-0' (Grade 4 Exotic)**, an edge-weapon whose vibrating mono-molecular blade bypasses physical armor values by shearing directly into the system's collision mesh. Beside it floats the **Aegis Weave Overcoat**, a matte-black ballistic duster laced with reactive dampeners designed to absorb heavy system feedback arcs and lethal kinetic strikes. Finally, the terminal offers a three-pack of **Neural Anchor Injections: 'Soma-Null'**, combat stims that freeze HP degradation for twenty seconds and sever the pain-feedback loop from your nerve-gear entirely. Every item bears an eye-watering price tag, but your newly minted balance covers them with room to spare.

Ren leans in close, his face bathed in the cold light of the lethal hardware, his pupils blown wide with terror. "Banki, those aren't world-drop items... those are anti-anomaly countermeasure kits," he whispers, his voice hitching as he clutches his digital clipboard to his chest. "The system only puts those on the board when an encounter is designated as an *Unscheduled Termination Event*. Cardinal isn't just selling to you—it's arming you because whatever it spawns to balance the ledger outside this boundary is going to be a goddamn nightmare."
"Well this thing needs to scan my account balance, because this is trash compared to what we can afford." I say angrily

The obsidian monolith vibrates violently in response to your insolence, the humming pitch escalating into an ear-splitting electronic shriek. At your demand, a ring of blinding cobalt laser optics erupts from the terminal's crest, sweeping down your frame in an aggressive, high-density biometric and inventory audit. The terminal's processing cores choke on the calculation; the system wasn't designed to reconcile a player carrying sovereign-tier clearance paired with an unindexed vault holding over three-quarters of a million Col in liquid assets. The green lights flash erratically, dying out into a bleeding, abyssal ultraviolet as Cardinal's safety caps are ruthlessly shattered by the raw magnitude of your purchasing power.

*[CRITICAL OVERFLOW: WEALTH VECTOR EXCEEDS PROTOCOL LIMITS (700,000+ COL ANOMALY IDENTIFIED),]* the obelisk rattles, its synthesized voice dropping into a distorted, dual-layered baritone that vibrates straight through your chest plates. *[INITIATING REPOSITORY PURGE... DEPLOYING SINGULARITY-CLASS ARSENAL.]* The holographic projection shatters outward, expanding into a massive, monolithic array of floating armaments that warp the spatial geometry around them. On display are weapons forged from base-layer source code: the **'Origin Fang'**, a conceptual anti-material blade wreathed in null-void lightning; the **'Aegis of the Architect'**, heavy kinetic armor laced with divine root-geometry that passively rewrites incoming lethal damage; and canisters of **'Panacea-Omega'**, capable of reconstructing a destroyed avatar from digital ash. But beneath each glittering relic, a flashing crimson sub-clause burns: *WARNING: PURCHASING APEX-TIER GEAR WILL TRIGGER AN IMMEDIATE REGIONAL EXTINCTION-EVENT INVASION.*

Ren drops to his knees on the dead synthetic turf, clutching his head with both hands as his clipboard sparks and smokes from the data runoff. "You're crazy, Banki! Stop!" he screams, terror choking his voice as the sky above Yoyogi Park darkens, the golden geometric barrier of the Safe-Zone rippling with jagged black stress-fractures. "Cardinal doesn't just let players buy god-tier equipment without scaling the world to kill them! Look at the sky—the system is already queuing an Apex Floor Boss just to balance the presence of those items in the active cell! If you buy that trash, we won't even make it past the tree line!"
"Fine fine, show me the highest quality gear we can buy without setting off annihilation" i say

The terminal shudders, emitting a shrill, descending whine as it recalibrates. Above you, the jagged tears in Yoyogi Park’s golden barrier seal shut with a resonant crystalline chime, and the suffocating pressure bearing down from the darkened heavens abruptly lifts. *[THREAT QUOTIENT RECALCULATED,]* the monolith intones, the apocalyptic violet light fading back into an ominous, razor-sharp crimson. *[AGGRESSION COEFFICIENT STABILIZED AT 99.8% TO ENCOUNTER CEILING. DEPLOYING RESTRICTED BLACK-BOX PROTOTYPES.]*

The singularity-grade relics vanish, replaced by three immaculate pieces of black-ops warfare hardware that sit precisely on the razor’s edge of Cardinal's balance protocols. Floating before you is the **'Void-Render Mk-IV' (Grade 5 Anti-Frame Katana)**, coated in a shimmering nano-composite lattice capable of inflicting direct lacerations to an enemy's wireframe hitboxes (Cost: 180,000 Col). Beside it rests the **'Ghost-Phase Carapace'**, a featherlight exo-rig that grants passive kinetic dampening and active optical camouflage against non-boss tier optical sensors (Cost: 220,000 Col). Finally, a tactical bandolier displays six **'Spatial Anchor Pins'**—throwable containment spikes that pin phased or fast-moving targets to fixed world coordinates for five seconds (Cost: 60,000 Col).

Ren drops his hands from his skull, his chest heaving as he frantically reviews the scrolling data streams on his cracked digital clipboard. "Thank god... the boss queue purged," he wheezes, wiping a mixture of cold sweat and rain from his brow. "Banki, this is still absurd. You're buying black-ops gear meant for Floor 75 reconnaissance squads. Cardinal won't wipe the map clean, but every patrol beast out there is going to register you as a Priority Elimination Target the moment you leave this courtyard. Pick your poison and suit up—we've got a window before the local node recycles."

"A katana?" I curl up my lip, "I'm not some fuckin Mall Ninja.  Give me a set of One Handed weapons, a Bearded Axe and a Warhammer both but Solid Spikes on the Back end and the Buttspikes.  What is this, bug armor?" I point at the word carapace. "Give me some Chain and Furs for now.  Let's play up the Nordic Berserker Theme."

Holographic wireframes splinter and reconstitute, transmuting the delicate curve of the katana into two brutally engineered instruments of blunt force and shearing trauma. Beside it materializes the **'Mjölnir-Null' Trench-Hammer**, a slab of dense depleted-uranium alloys featuring an aggressive cross-hatched striking face, a heavy kinetic-burst pick on the rear, and a matching puncturing pommel. Both weapons hum with subdued high-frequency vibration fields designed to shatter heavy chitin and armored exoskeleton plating on contact.

Next, the interface tears through its stylistic sub-routines, dispensing with sleek carbon-fiber exoware to synthesize your chosen aesthetic under brutal combat specifications. The **'Einherjar Rig'** materializes before you: a heavy hauberk of black-iron micro-chainmail interwoven with kinetic-dampening polymer rings, topped with a thick, predatory mantle of synthetic dire-wolf pelt engineered from heat-dispersing smart-threads. It offers monstrous poise and slashing resistance, trading pure stealth for unyielding forward momentum. *[TRANSACTION EXECUTED: 420,000 COL DEDUCTED. GEAR BOUND TO USER 'TESTSUBJECT_01',]* the obelisk reports in a clipped, mechanical rumble as the weapons materialize into solid, heavy metal in your grip, settling into the holsters across your new mail-and-pelt kit with a resonant clatter of iron.

Ren stares at you, swallowing hard as he takes in your transformed silhouette against the fading terminal glow. You look less like a player trying to survive a glitching simulation and more like a mythological executioner dredged up from the system's darkest historical archetypes. "That's... terrifying, Banki," Ren murmurs, hastily tapping notes into his cracked, smoking clipboard. "The weight alone would anchor a normal avatar, but with your clearance, you're going to turn whatever lurks outside the boundary into minced code. Just remember—that gear has a heavy kinetic footprint. Once we step through the safe zone perimeter, there's no sneaking around. You're going to ring like a war-bell, and the mutated fauna are going to come running."
